result.summary: The image shows a narrow urban residential street with continuous sidewalks on both sides and buildings situated directly at the sidewalk edge. While the narrow street width naturally limits vehicle speeds, the environment lacks marked pedestrian crossings, traffic calming measures, and physical buffers like street trees.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: There are no visible marked crosswalks for pedestrians to safely cross the street within the visible block.

hazards.name: Visual obstructions from parked vehicles
hazards.description: Large parked vehicles, such as the black van on the left, can obscure sightlines between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks at intersections to clearly define pedestrian space and improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) at crossing points to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planters
interventions.description: Add street trees or planters to provide a physical and psychological buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a wide, well-maintained sidewalk but is dominated by a large mid-block driveway serving a parking garage. The lack of a buffer between the walkway and the roadway, combined with blind spots created by the building edges at the driveway exit, presents significant conflict points.

hazards.name: Driveway Conflict Point
hazards.description: A large, gated driveway crosses the sidewalk, creating a point where vehicles and pedestrians must share space.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the image, crossing the sidewalk between the two buildings.

hazards.name: Blind Exit
hazards.description: The building walls extend directly to the sidewalk edge at the driveway, creating poor sightlines for drivers exiting the garage and pedestrians approaching the crossing.
hazards.location_in_image: The corners of the brick and metal buildings where they meet the driveway.

interventions.title: Continuous Sidewalk Treatment
interventions.description: Maintain the sidewalk material and elevation across the driveway to reinforce pedestrian priority and encourage slower vehicle speeds.

interventions.title: Visual and Audible Warnings
interventions.description: Install mirrors or sensor-activated lights/alarms to alert pedestrians of exiting vehicles and vice versa.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Furniture Zone
interventions.description: Introduce a buffer zone with street trees or planters to separate the walkway from the roadway and improve the pedestrian experience.

result.summary: The image depicts a narrow urban street with multi-story buildings and parallel parking on both sides. Pedestrian infrastructure is limited to narrow sidewalks that are frequently obstructed by utility poles, though a marked crosswalk is visible at the distant intersection.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles are located directly within the narrow sidewalk, significantly reducing the effective walking width and creating barriers for those with mobility aids.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both the left and right sidewalks.

hazards.name: Restricted Sight Lines
hazards.description: Parked vehicles extend close to the intersection, which can obscure pedestrians from the view of approaching drivers at the crosswalk.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) at the intersection to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and motorists.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening
interventions.description: Widen the sidewalks to provide a clear, unobstructed path of travel that accommodates utility infrastructure without impeding pedestrian flow.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to ensure clear sight lines for all road users.
